catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner, governance engine, and agent telemetry/skills framework.
analysis_limits: Repository inspected via file manifest, directory structure, pyproject.toml, and key symbol references.
Skill markdown specifications are observed in the directory tree without full prompt body extraction.

system_map.overview: CAS acts as an agentic continuous architecture orchestrator that enforces architectural compliance, reconciles changes across repositories using agent skills, monitors agent cost and activity via multi-harness telemetry adapters, and provides structured LLM interaction.

agents.name: verifier
agents.role: Independent verification and audit subagent inspecting compliance, rules, and architecture artifacts.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Agentic reconciliation agent that merges architectural governance specifications and steering rules.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: State machine transition controller governing state, lifecycle exceptions, and action execution.

orchestration.description: Sequential pipeline execution is driven by FlowRunner and GovernanceActionEngine, combined with distributed specialised agent skills in .agents/skills invoked via CLI or IDE agent harnesses.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provider-agnostic LLM interface supporting multi-model invocation with standardized retry and mock capabilities.

tools_and_integrations.name: CAS Skills Suite
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Packaged tool skills for drawing generation, rule auditing, feature mutation, and archgov review synchronization.

tools_and_integrations.name: AgentTelemetryAdapter
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Normalizes telemetry spans, token counts, and USD cost estimation across multiple agent runtime harnesses.

state_and_memory.description: File-based architectural knowledge repository (cas-knowledge) persisting decisions, rules, evolution maps, and trace logs.
Runtime context and rule execution evaluations managed during runner lifecycle.

patterns.name: Multi-Harness Agent Telemetry Normalization

tool_protocols.notes: Spans capture tool execution and LLM completion across diverse agent platforms.

optimisation_targets.notes: Tracks model usage, token expenditure, and execution epochs uniformly.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows developers to choose their agent runtime while centralising observability and spend limits.

patterns.summary: Decouple agent execution runtimes from cost and health telemetry by introducing runtime-specific adapters that normalize spans into a standard telemetry model.
patterns.intent: Aggregate trace metrics, token usage, and cost estimation across heterogeneous agent environments (e.g. Claude Code, Antigravity, coding CLI agents).
patterns.context: Agent execution happens across diverse IDE plugins, CLIs, and automated pipelines, each producing disparate trace formats.
forces: Different agent harnesses emit distinct telemetry schema formats
Financial and health tracking require unified cost and span aggregations
Adapters must gracefully infer providers when metadata is incomplete
patterns.solution: Define an AgentTelemetrySpan data class and implement specialized adapters (ClaudeCodeTelemetryAdapter, AntigravityTelemetryAdapter, CodingAgentTelemetryAdapter) that ingest external traces and map them to unified spans with USD cost calculations.
implementation_signals: Multiple Adapter classes subclassing or implementing span mapping methods
Centralized estimate_agent_cost_usd and _normalize_iso conversion helpers

evidence.note: Defines distinct adapters normalising trace spans from different coding agent ecosystems.

benefits: Uniform monitoring and auditing across varied developer agent tooling
Accurate cost tracking and token accounting across model providers
costs: Adapter maintenance overhead as external agent telemetry logs change
Heuristic provider inference can misattribute tokens if headers are missing
failure_modes: Incompatible timestamp formatting leading to dropped telemetry entries
Unrecognized model names causing zero-cost estimation

patterns.reuse_notes: Extract the adapter interface and pricing dictionary into a shared library for any system orchestrating multiple agent CLI tools.

patterns.name: File-Backed Architectural Knowledge Blackboard

tool_protocols.notes: Agents read and write markdown and YAML/JSON templates in git-tracked knowledge trees.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enforces transparent version-controlled memory accessible to humans and agents alike.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Git-backed files prevent black-box memory drift and allow human PR reviews on agent artifacts.

patterns.summary: Use a structured, version-controlled filesystem as a shared blackboard for agent memory, decision logs, heuristics, and runtime evaluation contexts.
patterns.intent: Maintain durable, human-auditable, and agent-accessible persistent memory without relying on proprietary vector or graph databases.
patterns.context: Autonomous and human-assisted agents make architecture decisions, generate diagrams, and record rules that must survive across workflow runs.
forces: Need persistent memory across stateless CI/CD runners
Humans must inspect and approve architectural decisions
Schema drift must be avoided across agent updates
patterns.solution: Organise cas-knowledge into structured subdirectories (global/decisions, global/rules, runtime/evaluations, templates/) governed by predefined Markdown and JSON templates that agents read and mutate.
implementation_signals: cas-knowledge folder hierarchy containing global, projects, runtime, and templates subdirectories
Rule context files like rule-context.json and execution-profile.yaml

evidence.note: Stores active rules context evaluated by agents during pipeline executions.
Templatized contract for agents promoting heuristics into patterns.

benefits: Complete version control history and diffability in Git
Zero operational overhead for external database hosting
costs: Git merge conflicts when multiple agents update files simultaneously
High I/O footprint for large trace evaluations
failure_modes: Malformed template parsing if an agent violates Markdown template schema

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt directory-based blackboard architectures for any agentic pipeline operating primarily in Git repositories.

patterns.name: Specialized Skill Directory Encapsulation

tool_protocols.notes: Skills define modular agent capability packages compatible with both Claude and custom runners.

optimisation_targets.notes: Encapsulates discrete domain capabilities into discoverable directories.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents are granted targeted capabilities per task rather than generic unbounded tools.

patterns.summary: Encapsulate agent capabilities into self-contained skill packages mirrored across agent runner environments (.agents and .claude).
patterns.intent: Modularize agent tools so that specific skills (e.g., diagram generator, module refactorer, review sync) can be maintained and tested independently.
patterns.context: Agents performing architectural governance require specific procedural knowledge and scripts to execute focused actions without polluting system prompt contexts.
forces: Monolithic system prompts exceed token budgets and degrade tool execution accuracy
Multiple agent environments (.claude, local CLI, CI workflows) require identical tool capabilities
patterns.solution: Define discrete skill directories containing operational scripts and prompts (.agents/skills/* and .claude/skills/*) and link them dynamically during workspace bootstrapping.
implementation_signals: Paired skill hierarchies in .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/
Bootstrap utilities linking or merging skills into runtime workspaces

evidence.note: Isolated skill package for generating and validating DrawIO architecture diagrams.
Provisions and synchronizes agent settings and skills into target workspaces.

benefits: Composable agent skill suites that can be enabled or audited per role
Clean separation between general agent prompt and tool-specific instructions
costs: Duplication or symlink management overhead between differing harness folder structures
failure_modes: Divergence between .agents/skills and .claude/skills if symlinks are severed

patterns.reuse_notes: Bundle tools as self-documenting skill subdirectories adhering to emerging standard agent skill directory conventions.

patterns.name: Independent Verifier Subagent

tool_protocols.notes: Verifier agent runs specialized verification passes over proposed artifacts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents confirmation bias by separating generation from verification.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Subagent holds dedicated evaluation role with distinct review prompts.

patterns.summary: Segregate mutation and validation responsibilities by defining a dedicated verifier subagent with specialized evaluation criteria.
patterns.intent: Eliminate self-review confirmation bias where the generating agent approves its own flawed architecture changes or hallucinations.
patterns.context: When agents propose architecture decisions or code mutations, relying solely on self-reflection fails on subtle boundary violations.
forces: Single agents are prone to justifying their prior generations during self-critique
Verification requires focused checklists and rules distinct from creative generation prompts
patterns.solution: Instantiate an explicit verifier subagent (.agents/subagents/verifier.md) tasked solely with auditing adherence to governance rules and finding compliance violations.
implementation_signals: Dedicated subagent configuration file (.agents/subagents/verifier.md and .claude/agents/verifier.md)
Compliance finding models consumed downstream by health scoring

evidence.note: Role specification defining independent verification agent.
Typed structures modeling findings and metrics output by verification passes.

benefits: Objective guardrails preventing unvetted architecture changes from merging
Separation of concerns between authoring skills and auditing skills
costs: Additional LLM roundtrips and latency for verifier execution
failure_modes: Verifier agent becoming overly pedantic or failing on unhandled schema extensions

patterns.reuse_notes: Deploy standalone verifier subagent profiles in code review and architecture pipelines.

patterns.name: State-Machine Governed Action Engine

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions gate execution actions deterministically.

optimisation_targets.notes: Restricts autonomous agent actions to valid state machine transitions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Strict state transitions prevent agents from executing illegal actions.

patterns.summary: Constrain autonomous agent decision execution within an explicit finite state transition registry that validates actions before mutating governance state.
patterns.intent: Prevent agents from skipping mandatory governance steps (e.g. promoting without prior verification or resolving without an approved action).
patterns.context: Governance actions must transition through known states (proposed, evaluated, approved, rejected, resolved) without unpredictable jumps.
forces: Unconstrained agents may execute destructive state updates out of order
Complex audit logs require deterministic proof of state transitions
patterns.solution: Implement a TransitionRegistry and GovernanceActionEngine that validate every requested GovernanceAction against valid origin and target states before execution.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry class tracking allowed source/target states
GovernanceActionEngine mediating execution and raising exceptions on invalid transitions

evidence.note: Registers valid transitions and dispatches actions through strict lifecycle validation.
Data models defining action schemas, exceptions, and execution results.

benefits: Guarantees that agents cannot bypass governance gates
Produces clear audit trails for automated compliance checks
costs: State registry must be updated whenever new governance actions are introduced
failure_modes: Unmapped state transitions raise GovernanceException, halting agent workflows

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a transition registry to restrict agent actions in any workflow where intermediate states represent approvals or safety gates.

patterns.name: Dual-Gateway Mockable LLM Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: Wraps LiteLLM completion calls with unified signature and fallback options.

optimisation_targets.notes: Permits unit testing without external API tokens or costs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Abstracts vendor lock-in behind a clean client interface.

patterns.summary: Provide a swappable LLM client boundary pairing a multi-provider LiteLLM client with an offline mock client to enable deterministic testing of agent logic.
patterns.intent: Decouple agentic business and governance logic from specific model providers and enable offline, reproducible CI tests without LLM API costs.
patterns.context: Agent workflows calling LLMs directly in test environments cause flaky tests, token expenses, and dependency on external API availability.
forces: Developers need multi-model flexibility (OpenAI, Anthropic, local models)
Automated CI test suites require deterministic, cost-free LLM completions
patterns.solution: Define LiteLLMClient wrapping LiteLLM for runtime calls and MockLLMClient implementing identical call signatures to inject canned or fixture responses during test runs.
implementation_signals: Pair of client modules: litellm_client.py and mock_client.py in src/cas_runner/llm/
Uniform completion method signatures returning standardized response objects

evidence.note: Production LLM wrapper handling multi-provider routing and token settings.
Mock client delivering predefined completions for agent testing.

benefits: Deterministic unit testing of complex agent reasoning pipelines
Zero token costs in CI validation builds
costs: Mock responses must be kept aligned with real model output variations
failure_modes: Mock client fails to simulate model streaming or timeout behaviors

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement dual real/mock clients early in any agentic system to ensure all agent flows remain testable in isolated CI environments.

patterns.name: Workspace Bootstrap Governance Injection

tool_protocols.notes: Injects governance configurations into agent settings JSON and system instruction files.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures every agent instance operating in the repository is bound by system rules.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automates rule provisioning so individual developer agents inherit corporate steering.

patterns.summary: Inject shared governance blocks, steering rules, and tool settings directly into developer agent configurations during workspace bootstrap.
patterns.intent: Ensure that IDE-based AI agents (such as Claude Code or custom agents) automatically adhere to organization-wide rules without manual copy-pasting.
patterns.context: Different developers launch AI agents locally; without automated bootstrap, agents hallucinate outside repository standards or ignore governance rules.
forces: Developer friction when manually configuring agent rule sets
Risk of overwriting custom developer settings with rigid central policies
patterns.solution: Provide a bootstrap command that merges a central CAS governance block and custom settings into local configuration files (.claude/settings.json, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) using deep merge logic.
implementation_signals: bootstrap, init_workspace, and merge_cas_governance_block functions in src/cas_runner/bootstrap.py
render_onboarding_checklist guiding setup validation

evidence.note: Merges governance blocks into target workspace configuration files.

benefits: Enforces standardized rules and guardrails across all local agent sessions
Reduces onboarding friction for new contributors
costs: Potential conflicts if developers maintain conflicting local settings
failure_modes: JSON parsing errors or clobbered custom settings if merge fails on non-standard formatting

patterns.reuse_notes: Use structured JSON/YAML merge routines to inject compliance prompts into local agent harness configs during repository setup.

patterns.name: Evidence-Derived Agentic Health Scoring

tool_protocols.notes: Computes health enumerations based on quantitative rule and metric evaluations.

optimisation_targets.notes: Determines system readiness based on concrete findings rather than LLM self-assessment.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Deterministic health scoring avoids hallucinated claims of system correctness.

patterns.summary: Compute system and governance health status through deterministic mathematical thresholds over collected compliance findings and trace metrics.
patterns.intent: Provide an unambiguous indicator of whether an agent-assisted system is healthy, degraded, or unhealthy without relying on vague LLM summaries.
patterns.context: Agent-driven refactoring and automated PR generation need automated gating criteria before deployment or publication.
forces: LLM self-evaluations tend to be overly optimistic
Raw violation counts need clear classification for CI pipeline gating
patterns.solution: Implement a health evaluation function that inspects GovernanceHealth metrics, computes error/warning densities, and yields discrete HealthStatus enums with explicit reason strings.
implementation_signals: HealthStatus enum (e.g., healthy, degraded, unhealthy) in health_model.py
calculate_health and get_health_reasons functions mapping metrics to status

evidence.note: Computes health status from quantitative metrics and outputs descriptive failure reasons.
Typed models tracking architectural health and risk indicators.

benefits: Consistent, deterministic quality gate for continuous architecture pipelines
Provides human-readable diagnostic messages explaining degradation
costs: Threshold heuristics (e.g. max warnings allowed) may need periodic calibration
failure_modes: Edge case metrics not mapped into health ranges leading to incorrect status reporting

patterns.reuse_notes: Combine discrete health enums with reason collectors to gate automated agent deployments in CI/CD workflows.

patterns.name: Pipeline Orchestration Flow Runner

tool_protocols.notes: Steps execute against shared flow execution context.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees ordered multi-step agent flow execution.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Orchestrator controls step order while steps execute domain-specific logic.

patterns.summary: Orchestrate multi-step agentic workflows sequentially via a dedicated FlowRunner that manages execution context and step lifecycles.
patterns.intent: Coordinate complex multi-phase agent tasks (e.g., ingestion, compliance checking, reconciliation, artifact generation) with predictable control flow.
patterns.context: Agent tasks require executing discrete steps in sequence where downstream steps depend on data generated by upstream steps.
forces: Autonomous agent loops without step boundaries can get trapped in repetitive reasoning loops
Shared state must be passed cleanly between distinct operational steps
patterns.solution: Define FlowRunner in src/cas_runner/runner.py which loads execution profiles, initialises state contexts, and triggers step execution in declared sequence.
implementation_signals: FlowRunner class in runner.py
Execution profile YAML configuration in cas-knowledge/runtime/execution-profile.yaml

evidence.note: Main pipeline execution engine orchestrating continuous architecture steps.
CLI entry point initiating runner execution with parsed flags.

benefits: Linear, predictable execution path enabling straightforward debugging and telemetry
Easy insertion of new steps into existing workflows
costs: Sequential execution may have higher wall-clock latency than fully parallel swarms
failure_modes: Unhandled step exception halts entire pipeline if fail-safe error handling is omitted

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a sequential FlowRunner pattern when workflow steps have strict data dependencies and require auditable boundaries.

patterns.name: Declarative Schema Governance Contracts

tool_protocols.notes: Pydantic and jsonschema define strict model contracts for all agent outputs and inputs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees agent inputs and outputs strictly conform to typed structures.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Strong data typing prevents schema drift and hallucinated output structures.

patterns.summary: Enforce strict typing and runtime schema validation on all agent outputs, governance actions, and telemetry using Pydantic and JSON Schema.
patterns.intent: Prevent unstructured or hallucinated agent output from propagating through the architecture pipeline.
patterns.context: Agents generating findings, health assessments, or actions can produce non-conforming JSON if not tightly bound by runtime validation.
forces: LLMs frequently emit near-compliant JSON with subtle field omissions or type mismatches
Downstream consumers require guaranteed field presence and types
patterns.solution: Define comprehensive Pydantic models (ResolutionResult, GovernanceAction, ComplianceFinding, TraceableMetric) that validate structured dictionaries immediately upon emission.
implementation_signals: Extensive Pydantic model definitions in src/cas_runner/governance/models.py
Dependencies on pydantic>=2.12.5 and jsonschema>=4.22.0 in pyproject.toml

evidence.note: Typed models defining strict contracts across all governance operations.
Includes pydantic and jsonschema as core runtime dependencies.

benefits: Early, deterministic failure when an agent generates non-conforming responses
Automatic serialisation, deserialisation, and OpenAPI/JSON-Schema documentation
costs: Requires validation retry handling when model outputs fail initial parsing
failure_modes: ValidationError raised during runtime execution if an LLM response deviates from schema

patterns.reuse_notes: Use Pydantic V2 models for all agentic tool arguments and structured generation targets.

anti_patterns.name: Heuristic Provider and Model Inference
symptoms: Telemetry parsing relies on guessing LLM providers via substring matches rather than explicit metadata.
Model cost calculations default to zero or fall back to generic rates when provider strings vary.

where_observed.note: Contains heuristic substring matching logic to guess the underlying LLM provider from span properties.

impact: Misattribution of token usage and incorrect financial cost reporting in multi-model environments.
Fragility whenever upstream agent harnesses rename or alias model identifier strings.
suggested_remediation: Require upstream agent telemetry harnesses to emit explicit provider and model identifiers in span attributes.
Reject or quarantine telemetry spans that lack authoritative provider metadata instead of guessing.

anti_patterns.name: Unpinned CI Agent Workflow Tool Installation
symptoms: CI workflow steps invoke package managers or agent harnesses with floating or unpinned versions.
Workflow validation checks must explicitly scan for unpinned installer commands.

where_observed.note: Explicitly scans workflows to block unpinned installations from introducing non-deterministic agent runtime behaviors.

impact: Silent drift in agent capabilities and syntax parsing across CI/CD execution runs.
Vulnerability to breaking changes or supply-chain compromises in third-party agent dependencies.
suggested_remediation: Enforce strict version pinning or lockfile validation in pre-commit and workflow validation hooks.
Package agent dependencies in immutable container images.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Integrated OpenTelemetry SDK alongside custom AgentTelemetrySpan adapters to record trace spans, model usage, and calculated USD spend across diverse developer agent tools.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Enables cross-team financial and operational tracking of AI assistant usage.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Multi-tier safety involving state-machine-controlled transition validation, independent verifier subagents, and Pydantic model validation on all actions.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Prevents runaway or unverified agent actions from being promoted to production knowledge bases.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Centralized estimate_agent_cost_usd function calculating per-span costs based on prompt and completion token prices.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Permits pipeline budget gating before high-token batch runs.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent agent writes reconciled if multiple agents execute merge operations on the cas-knowledge blackboard simultaneously?
open_questions.why_it_matters: File-based blackboards can suffer race conditions or merge conflicts if multiple GitHub Actions or local agents commit changes concurrently.
open_questions.evidence_gap: The file structure shows concurrent project directories, but Git lock mechanisms or retry semantics in AgenticMerger were not directly inspected in the manifest snippet.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Inspect src/cas_runner/governance/agentic_merger.py for lockfile handling or git pull rebase logic.

open_questions.question: What is the runtime discovery mechanism for skills in .agents/skills during FlowRunner execution?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Understanding whether skills are invoked via MCP, local subprocesses, or LLM tool-calling blocks is key to mapping external tool boundaries.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Skills are present in the directory structure, but FlowRunner step execution mechanics require inspection of src/cas_runner/runner.py.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Examine src/cas_runner/runner.py for dynamic tool registration or CLI subprocess invocation.
